retained_original_metadata.title: Determinantal evaluation of the N-variable complex Gamma sum-integral with pole-separated contours and the explicit unbarred/barred convergence bounds
retained_original_metadata.author: Sergey E. Derkachov; Alexander N. Manashov
retained_original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The direct proof transforms a multidimensional discrete-continuous integral into a determinant of Mellin moments. It factors a coupled residue/discrete sum into two multivariate hypergeometric sums, then resolves the permutation signs and a sine-sum cancellation to obtain the Gamma product. Control of contour poles, absolute convergence and the two independent residue sectors is essential beyond applying an ordinary one-dimensional Barnes identity.

proof_review.note: Read all of Section2.3 for identity2.3a, together with the absolute-convergence estimates and moment-determinant reduction. The two residue-sector factorization and subsequent finite-permutation sign simplification are supplied in full. Milne U(n) Gauss summation and the final finite sine identity are explicitly identified established background. Select only the explicit residue-proof subdomain(2.12), retaining pole-separated contours, integer index convention and the independent barred parameter pair of(2.1); do not include2.3b, whose author proof only highlights differences, or the final broader analytic-continuation assertion.

retained_original_metadata.statement_scope: Identity(2.3a) for N>=1, integer discrete parts of all u,z,w as fixed in Section2.1, Gamma(u,bar_u)=Gamma(u)/Gamma(1-bar_u) with bar_u a paired parameter, not assumed complex conjugation. Use contours separating the two specified pole strings and the stricter explicit proof conditions sum Re(z_k+w_k)<1 AND sum Re(bar_z_k+bar_w_k)<1 from(2.12), in the absolutely convergent pole-separated regime of(2.8). The conclusion is exactly the displayed Gamma-product evaluation, including 1/N! and sum/integration measure.
